canonical_text: The Company shall pay the Employee a gross annual salary, payable in twelve equal monthly instalments, subject to applicable deductions as per prevailing tax laws.
typical_range: Varies by role and industry; standard structure is monthly payment with tax deductions
source_note: Composite of publicly available standard employment templates
stricter_signals: deferred payment beyond monthly cycle
salary reduction clauses
performance-linked base pay reduction

canonical_text: Either party may terminate this agreement by giving thirty (30) days written notice.
typical_range: 30-60 days for non-managerial roles; 60-90 days for managerial/senior roles
source_note: Composite of publicly available standard employment templates
stricter_signals: notice period exceeding 90 days
asymmetric notice (longer for employee than employer)
notice buy-out at more than one month salary
garden leave with restricted activity

canonical_text: The Employee shall be on probation for a period of six (6) months from the date of joining. During probation, either party may terminate with fifteen (15) days notice.
typical_range: 3-6 months probation; 7-15 days notice during probation
source_note: Composite of publicly available standard employment templates
stricter_signals: probation exceeding 6 months
automatic extension of probation without criteria
no notice required from employer during probation
reduced benefits during extended probation

canonical_text: The Employee agrees to serve the Company for a minimum period of one (1) year from the date of completion of training. In the event of early separation, the Employee shall repay a proportionate amount of the training costs.
typical_range: 1-2 years bond period; proportionate repayment based on time served
source_note: Composite of publicly available standard employment templates
stricter_signals: bond period exceeding 2 years
fixed penalty amount without proportional reduction
bond applies to termination for cause
no itemization of training costs
bond amount exceeds 50% of annual salary
bond on general onboarding rather than specialized training

canonical_text: The Employee shall not engage in any competing business during the term of employment.
typical_range: During-employment non-compete is standard; post-termination non-compete is unusual in India
source_note: Composite of publicly available standard employment templates; Indian legal practice
stricter_signals: post-termination restriction of any duration
geographic scope covering all of India or multiple states
broad definition of 'competing business'
applies regardless of reason for termination
includes indirect engagement or consulting

canonical_text: During the term of employment, the Employee shall not solicit or entice away any employee, consultant, or client of the Company.
typical_range: During-employment is standard; post-termination 6-12 months is common but enforceability varies
source_note: Composite of publicly available standard employment templates
stricter_signals: post-termination restriction exceeding 12 months
covers all contacts rather than just clients you directly worked with
includes passive receipt of applications from former colleagues
covers vendors and partners in addition to clients

canonical_text: The Employee shall maintain confidentiality of all proprietary information during and after employment.
typical_range: Perpetual for trade secrets; 2-5 years for general confidential information
source_note: Composite of publicly available standard employment templates
stricter_signals: overly broad definition of confidential information covering publicly available knowledge
no carve-outs for independently developed information
criminal liability provisions beyond civil remedies
restrictions on discussing employment terms/compensation

canonical_text: Intellectual property created in the course of employment and related to the Company's business shall belong to the Company.
typical_range: Work-related IP assignment is standard; scope should be limited to company business
source_note: Composite of publicly available standard employment templates
stricter_signals: covers all IP created during employment period regardless of relation to work
no carve-out for prior inventions
no carve-out for personal projects on own time and resources
includes moral rights waiver
covers IP created using personal resources outside work hours

canonical_text: Either party may terminate this agreement by giving the stipulated notice period. The Company may terminate immediately for cause, including but not limited to material breach, misconduct, or conviction of a criminal offence.
typical_range: Mutual termination with notice; immediate termination for defined cause
source_note: Composite of publicly available standard employment templates
stricter_signals: unilateral termination right for employer without cause and without notice
vague or undefined 'cause' categories
no opportunity to cure before termination
forfeiture of all benefits on termination for any reason
termination linked to subjective performance assessment

canonical_text: In the event of breach by the Employee, the Employee shall pay the Company reasonable damages as a genuine pre-estimate of loss, not exceeding the amount specified.
typical_range: Amount should reflect genuine pre-estimate of actual loss; subject to court reduction under Section 74 ICA
source_note: Composite of publicly available standard employment templates; Indian Contract Act s.74 jurisprudence
stricter_signals: penalty amount exceeding 6 months salary
no cap on damages
penalty for breach of non-compete (which may itself be void)
cumulative penalties for multiple breach types
penalty without any relationship to actual loss

canonical_text: The Employee shall indemnify the Company against any losses arising from the Employee's wilful misconduct or negligence in the performance of duties.
typical_range: Indemnity limited to wilful misconduct or gross negligence; should not cover ordinary course of business errors
source_note: Composite of publicly available standard employment templates
stricter_signals: uncapped indemnity
indemnity for ordinary negligence
indemnity surviving termination indefinitely
indemnity covering third-party claims not caused by employee
reverse indemnity (employee indemnifies for employer's decisions)

canonical_text: The parties shall attempt to resolve any dispute through good faith negotiation before resorting to formal proceedings.
typical_range: Negotiation → Mediation → Arbitration/Litigation is standard escalation
source_note: Composite of publicly available standard employment templates
stricter_signals: mandatory arbitration with employer-appointed arbitrator
waiver of right to access labour courts
dispute resolution in a distant city
shortened limitation periods
cost-bearing provisions that discourage dispute filing

canonical_text: Disputes shall be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts in [City], [State].
typical_range: Courts at the employer's principal place of business; should allow employee's location for employment disputes
source_note: Composite of publicly available standard employment templates
stricter_signals: jurisdiction in a city far from where employee works
exclusive jurisdiction waiving employee's right to file at their own location
foreign jurisdiction clause

canonical_text: Any dispute arising under this agreement shall be referred to arbitration under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996. The arbitration shall be conducted by a sole arbitrator mutually appointed by the parties.
typical_range: Sole arbitrator, mutually appointed; seat at employer's principal place of business
source_note: Composite of publicly available standard employment templates; Arbitration and Conciliation Act 1996
stricter_signals: employer appoints sole arbitrator unilaterally
three-arbitrator panel (expensive for employee)
arbitration in a distant location
employee bears all arbitration costs
confidentiality clause preventing disclosure of outcome

canonical_text: The normal working hours shall be eight (8) hours per day, five days a week, subject to the requirements of the role.
typical_range: 8-9 hours per day, 5-6 days per week; overtime provisions per Factories Act / SE Act
source_note: Composite of publicly available standard employment templates; State SE Acts
stricter_signals: unlimited working hours obligation
waiver of overtime compensation
mandatory availability outside work hours without compensation
no cap on weekly hours

canonical_text: The Employee shall be entitled to annual leave as per the Company's leave policy, which shall not be less than the statutory minimum.
typical_range: 15-24 days annual leave; 12 days casual leave; 12 days sick leave (varies by state)
source_note: Composite of publicly available standard employment templates; State SE Acts
stricter_signals: leave entitlement below statutory minimum
forfeiture of unused leave without encashment
leave approval solely at employer's discretion with no guaranteed minimum
no carry-forward provisions

canonical_text: The Employee shall be eligible for benefits as per the Company's policies, including provident fund contributions as required by law.
typical_range: PF, ESI (if applicable), gratuity after 5 years, medical insurance (employer policy)
source_note: Composite of publicly available standard employment templates; EPF Act, ESI Act
stricter_signals: exclusion from statutory benefits
benefits contingent on meeting performance targets
clawback of benefits on early separation
no clarity on gratuity eligibility

canonical_text: This agreement may be amended by mutual written consent of both parties.
typical_range: Mutual written consent is standard
source_note: Composite of publicly available standard employment templates
stricter_signals: unilateral amendment right for employer
amendment by mere notice without consent
deemed consent if employee continues working after policy change
broad reservation of right to change 'any terms at any time'

canonical_text: If any provision of this agreement is held to be invalid or unenforceable, the remaining provisions shall continue in full force and effect.
typical_range: Standard boilerplate; included in most agreements
source_note: Composite of publicly available standard employment templates
stricter_signals: no severability clause (rare but risky)
blue-pencil clause allowing court to rewrite terms rather than strike them

canonical_text: During the probation period, either party may terminate this agreement by giving seven (7) days written notice.
typical_range: 7-15 days during probation
source_note: Composite of publicly available standard employment templates
stricter_signals: no notice required from employer during probation
full notice period applying during probation
probation termination without any reason or notice

canonical_text: In the event of early separation, the Employee shall repay a proportionate amount of the documented training costs, calculated based on the remaining bond period.
typical_range: Proportional reduction is considered fair practice; full amount recovery is stricter
source_note: Composite of publicly available standard employment templates; Section 74 ICA jurisprudence
stricter_signals: no proportional reduction
recovery of amounts unrelated to training (e.g., salary, relocation)
bond applying to employer-initiated termination
bond on mandatory industry certifications

canonical_text: During the term of employment, the Employee shall devote their full working time and attention to the Company's business and shall not engage in any other employment or business without prior written consent.
typical_range: Full-time exclusivity during employment is standard for full-time roles
source_note: Composite of publicly available standard employment templates
stricter_signals: prohibition on all outside activities including volunteering
prohibition surviving into personal time for non-competing activities
no exception for pre-existing personal projects

canonical_text: The Employee shall disclose any prior inventions or intellectual property at the time of joining. Such prior inventions shall remain the property of the Employee unless incorporated into the Company's products or services.
typical_range: Prior invention disclosure and carve-out is best practice
source_note: Composite of publicly available standard employment templates; US/India tech industry practice
stricter_signals: no prior invention carve-out
all prior IP deemed assigned upon incorporation without additional compensation
no process for resolving ownership disputes

canonical_text: The Company may terminate this agreement immediately for cause, including material breach of agreement, wilful misconduct, conviction of a criminal offence, or gross negligence. The Employee shall be given a reasonable opportunity to be heard before termination for cause.
typical_range: Defined cause categories with opportunity to be heard is standard
source_note: Composite of publicly available standard employment templates; principles of natural justice
stricter_signals: no opportunity to be heard
subjective cause categories ('unsatisfactory performance' without metrics)
termination for cause includes breach of any company policy (even minor)
no severance or notice pay on termination for cause

canonical_text: Confidential Information means any non-public information relating to the Company's business, including trade secrets, customer lists, financial data, and technical know-how, but excluding information that is publicly available or independently developed.
typical_range: Defined scope with standard exclusions (public domain, independently developed, required by law)
source_note: Composite of publicly available standard employment templates
stricter_signals: no exclusions for publicly available information
includes information the employee already knew
covers information learned after termination
penalty for inadvertent disclosure equal to wilful disclosure

canonical_text: The Company may transfer the Employee to any of its offices within India with reasonable notice and relocation support.
typical_range: Transfer with 30 days notice and relocation allowance is standard
source_note: Composite of publicly available standard employment templates
stricter_signals: transfer without notice
no relocation support
transfer as a punitive measure
mandatory international relocation without consent

canonical_text: This agreement constitutes the entire agreement between the parties and supersedes all prior negotiations, representations, or agreements.
typical_range: Standard boilerplate; commonly included
source_note: Composite of publicly available standard employment templates
stricter_signals: oral modifications permitted (creates uncertainty)
merger clause that eliminates verbal promises made during hiring

canonical_text: This agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of India.
typical_range: Indian law for India-based employment is standard
source_note: Composite of publicly available standard employment templates
stricter_signals: foreign governing law for India-based employment
choice of law that overrides mandatory Indian employment protections

canonical_text: Neither party shall be liable for failure to perform obligations due to circumstances beyond reasonable control, including natural disasters, pandemics, and government actions.
typical_range: Standard force majeure clause; increasingly includes pandemic provisions post-COVID
source_note: Composite of publicly available standard employment templates
stricter_signals: employer can suspend salary during force majeure without limit
force majeure allows unilateral termination without notice
no employee protections during force majeure period

canonical_text: The Company shall collect, process, and store the Employee's personal data in accordance with applicable data protection laws and the Company's privacy policy.
typical_range: Standard data privacy clause; should reference DPDP Act 2023 provisions
source_note: Composite of publicly available standard employment templates; Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023
stricter_signals: blanket consent to data processing without purpose limitation
data sharing with third parties without notification
no right to access or correct personal data
data retention beyond employment term without justification

canonical_text: This offer is contingent upon successful completion of background verification. Any material misrepresentation in your application may result in termination.
typical_range: Standard contingency clause; verification typically covers education, employment history, criminal records
source_note: Composite of publicly available standard employment templates
stricter_signals: background check scope includes social media monitoring
verification of family members
indefinite right to re-verify after joining
termination for minor discrepancies

canonical_text: The Employee shall be eligible for gratuity as per the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972, upon completion of five years of continuous service.
typical_range: Statutory entitlement after 5 years; 15 days wages per year of service
source_note: Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972; publicly available employment templates
stricter_signals: forfeiture of gratuity on termination for cause (beyond statutory grounds)
calculation on basic salary only when CTC includes substantial allowances
non-payment or delayed payment provisions

canonical_text: The probation period may be extended by up to three (3) months at the Company's discretion, with written notice to the Employee citing specific performance areas for improvement.
typical_range: One extension of 1-3 months with clear criteria is standard
source_note: Composite of publicly available standard employment templates
stricter_signals: unlimited extensions
no criteria for extension
reduced pay during extended probation
no confirmation deemed denial

canonical_text: Upon termination, the Employee shall return all Company property, complete knowledge transfer, and obtain clearance from relevant departments.
typical_range: Standard exit process; final settlement within 30-45 days
source_note: Composite of publicly available standard employment templates
stricter_signals: withholding final settlement pending return of property (may violate wage laws)
no timeline for final settlement
mandatory non-disparagement post-exit
exit interview testimony usable against employee

canonical_text: The Employee may be eligible for an annual performance bonus based on individual and Company performance, at the Company's discretion.
typical_range: Discretionary bonus based on performance; 10-30% of CTC for mid-level roles
source_note: Composite of publicly available standard employment templates
stricter_signals: bonus clawback for employees who resign within N months of payout
no minimum bonus guarantee when described as part of CTC
bonus contingent on factors entirely outside employee's control

canonical_text: In lieu of serving the notice period, either party may pay the equivalent of the notice period salary to the other party.
typical_range: Mutual notice buy-out at basic salary or gross salary
source_note: Composite of publicly available standard employment templates
stricter_signals: buy-out at CTC including benefits (inflates cost)
employer can mandate serving full notice without buy-out option
employee must serve but employer can buy-out (asymmetric)

canonical_text: The Employee may engage in outside activities that do not conflict with the Company's business interests, provided prior written approval is obtained.
typical_range: Prior approval requirement is standard for full-time roles
source_note: Composite of publicly available standard employment templates
stricter_signals: blanket prohibition on all outside activities including volunteering
no approval process (just prohibition)
includes activities during personal time that don't compete

canonical_text: The Employee shall comply with the Company's Code of Conduct and all applicable policies as amended from time to time.
typical_range: Standard compliance clause; policies should be made available to employee
source_note: Composite of publicly available standard employment templates
stricter_signals: policies not provided at time of signing
retroactive application of new policies
termination for violation of any policy regardless of severity

canonical_text: The Company shall provide group medical insurance coverage for the Employee and their dependents as per the Company's insurance policy.
typical_range: Group medical insurance covering employee + family; ₹3-5 lakh coverage is standard for mid-level
source_note: Composite of publicly available standard employment templates
stricter_signals: no insurance coverage
employee-only coverage without dependents
coverage significantly below industry standard
coverage void during probation

canonical_text: The Company shall make contributions to the Employee's Provident Fund account as required under the Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952.
typical_range: 12% of basic salary by both employer and employee; statutory requirement
source_note: EPF Act, 1952; publicly available employment templates
stricter_signals: PF contribution on lower basic component (legal but disadvantageous)
opting out of PF without employee consent
VPF restrictions

canonical_text: The Employee may resign by submitting a written resignation to the Company. The notice period shall commence from the date of acceptance of the resignation by the Company.
typical_range: Written resignation with notice period starting from submission date
source_note: Composite of publicly available standard employment templates
stricter_signals: notice period starts only from acceptance (delays departure)
Company may reject resignation (unusual)
mandatory cooling-off period before resignation is effective
resignation requires multiple approvals
